title: The Cortex Map Is Drawn Twice

scenes.tts: In an adult mouse, a patch of cortex near the middle maps the whiskers. A patch near the back maps what the eyes see. In the embryo, the sheet that will hold both looks the same from front to back. It shows no clear borders. So where do the areas come from? The process is called arealization.
scenes.visual: Adult mouse map (whiskers, eyes) under a blank embryonic sheet; a question mark between them.
scenes.narration: In an adult mouse, a patch of cortex near the middle maps the whiskers. A patch near the back maps what the eyes see. In the embryo, the sheet that will hold both looks the same from front to back. It shows no clear borders. So where do the areas come from? The process is called arealization.

scenes.tts: Cells in the sheet do differ by position. Progenitors are the cells that divide to make neurons. They hold transcription factors, proteins that switch genes on or off. In the mouse, two of them form opposing gradients. E M X two is highest at the back. Pax six is highest at the front. Each progenitor reads its position from the mix it holds.
scenes.visual: Sheet splits into two bars; orange and blue opposing gradients; a cell slides along and reads the mix.
scenes.caption: Cells in the sheet do differ by position. Progenitors are the cells that divide to make neurons. They hold transcription factors, proteins that switch genes on or off. In the mouse, two of them form opposing gradients. Emx2 is highest at the back. Pax6 is highest at the front. Each progenitor reads its position from the mix it holds.
scenes.narration: Cells in the sheet do differ by position. Progenitors are the cells that divide to make neurons. They hold transcription factors, proteins that switch genes on or off. In the mouse, two of them form opposing gradients. Emx2 is highest at the back. Pax6 is highest at the front. Each progenitor reads its position from the mix it holds.

scenes.tts: Does the mix matter? Remove one factor and look. The areas are read from marker genes at birth. Without E M X two, the front areas expanded toward the back, and the visual area shrank. Without working Pax six, the shift went the other way. Raise E M X two, keeping its slope, and the map moves the opposite way from the knockout. A factor whose loss and excess move a border in opposite directions is allocating territory.
scenes.visual: Area map shifts with no Emx2, no Pax6, and extra Emx2; each case resets first.

scenes.tts: The gradients need a source of position. At the front, a signal called F G F eight is released. Think of it as a lamp at the front of a room. Cells read how bright it is to judge how far forward they sit. A landmark shows the effect: the barrel field, one cluster of cells for each whisker. Add a second source at the back, and a partial second barrel field forms behind the first. Block the signal at the front, and the barrel field moves toward the front.
scenes.visual: Yellow source glows at the front; barrel field moves with second source at back and with blocker at front.

scenes.tts: Genes sketch the map, but input shapes much of it. Thalamic axons bring signals from the eyes, ears and skin. In rats, fetal visual cortex was grafted into somatosensory cortex. Whisker axons grew into the graft, and the graft formed barrels. Yet in mice where thalamic axons never reach the cortex, area markers still had their normal borders at birth. The sketch forms without input.
scenes.visual: Thalamic axons reach the map; visual graft forms barrels; axons stopped short, borders still there.
scenes.narration: Genes sketch the map, but input shapes much of it. Thalamic axons bring signals from the eyes, ears and skin. In rats, fetal visual cortex was grafted into somatosensory cortex. Whisker axons grew into the graft, and the graft formed barrels. Yet in mice where thalamic axons never reach the cortex, area markers still had their normal borders at birth. The sketch forms without input.

scenes.tts: So the map is drawn twice. First comes a sketch from the sheet. Gradients and a signal from the edge set where the borders fall. Then comes a refined copy, shaped by the thalamic input. Move the signal, and the sketch moves. Keep this rule: position sketches the map, and input then refines it.
scenes.visual: Sketch bar with gradients above a refined bar with input; borders shift as the signal weakens.
